5 Wounded as Russia Strikes Dnipropetrovsk Region — Russian armed forces attacked two districts of Ukraine’s Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 40 times with drones and artillery on Tuesday, wounding five people. A 65-year-old man remains in critical condition after strikes hit residential and commercial buildings.

The Battle Beyond the Battlefield: Winning Back Hearts — Ukraine’s wartime image in the West, once bolstered by its heroic resistance, is eroding — partly due to a historical dispute with Poland over the UPA’s legacy. After Zelensky named a unit after UPA figures tied to WWII massacres of Poles, tensions flared. The piece argues Ukraine needs pragmatic, durable solutions on historical memory, not nationalist rhetoric, to protect its EU membership prospects.

EU Agency Halts Venice Biennale Funding Over Russia’s Return — The EU's education and culture agency has terminated a €2 million (roughly $2.2 million) grant to the Venice Biennale after organizers allowed Russia's pavilion to reopen. Ukraine and more than twenty European countries had pushed for Russia's exclusion.

Secret Baku Talks Confirmed Between German and Russian Officials — Azerbaijani President confirmed that former German and Russian officials secretly met in Baku on July 12–14 to discuss Russia's war against Ukraine. However, German Chancellor said his government had no involvement and was unaware of the meeting taking place.

Black Sea Naval War Heats Up as Russia, Ukraine Trade Fiery Attacks vs Civilian Ships — Ukraine and Russia have escalated Black Sea attacks on civilian shipping. Ukrainian drones struck tankers at Russia’s KTK terminal, while Russian missiles hit the grain ship Golden Leo, killing 10 in likely the war’s deadliest attack on a merchant vessel.

Gas Tanker En Route to Ukraine Struck Off Romanian Coast in Potential Russian Strike — Romania’s president said the Liberia-flagged LPG tanker Gas Lisbon was struck in Romanian waters late Monday, injuring three crew members. Romania and Ukraine blamed Russia for the attack, the latest in a string of strikes on vessels as both Kyiv and Moscow have intensified strikes in the Black Sea.

Ukraine Hits Russian MiG-29, Pantsir System at Kursk Airfield in $45M Blow — Ukraine says its forces hit a Russian MiG-29 fighter jet and a Pantsir-S1 air defense system at the Khalino airfield in Russia’s Kursk region. Drone footage released by the military appears to show the operation, though its authenticity has not been independently verified.

Russia Adds More Rassvet Satellites, Attempting to Build Its Own ‘Starlink’ — Russia has launched a second batch of Rassvet satellites, increasing its Starlink-like constellation to about 40 orbiters. Analysts say the network remains far from military readiness, as Moscow will need several hundred satellites before it can provide reliable battlespace C3.

Waiting for AFU Chief’s Dismissal: Who Could Replace Him? — As protests in Kyiv increasingly target Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrsky, opinion within the military is divided, with some backing calls for change while others argue that replacing the army’s leadership during wartime would be a dangerous mistake. Meanwhile, President Volodymyr Zelensky is reportedly meeting with six senior commanders who are viewed as potential successors, though no decision on Syrsky’s future has been made.
CARTOON: What Happened to “All That Gas?” — Serhiy Kolyada’s ironic take on the latest international events.

Kremlin Says No News on Patel's October Trip to Russia — The Kremlin said it has no news of FBI Director Kash Patel’s rumored October trip to Russia hosted by the FSB, before adding that it cannot share the information even if it has it. Politico, which reported the rumored trip, noted the peculiar timing as it coincides with public clashes between Washington and Moscow over the war in Ukraine.

New UK Defense Chief Backs Ukraine, Inherits Strained Armed Forces — Newly appointed UK Secretary of Defence Wes Streeting vowed “steadfast” support for Ukraine after assuming his new role on Monday. Despite the optimistic tone, questions remain as to whether the former health secretary is able to reverse course following decades of underfunding for the British military as his predecessor resigned over funding rows.

Russian Warship Conducts Live-Fire Drill Off Britain’s Plymouth — The Russian frigate Neustrashimy conducted a 30-minute live-fire exercise in international waters about 40 nautical miles off the British coastal city of Plymouth on Monday. The drill coincided with the appointment of Britain’s new prime minister and followed a string of incidents involving Russian vessels near British waters.

Crimea Plunges Into Darkness Again as Fresh Blasts Hit Russian Energy Grid — New explosions struck occupied Crimea overnight, damaging key power substations and triggering fresh blackouts. As Ukraine’s campaign against Russian energy infrastructure intensifies, occupation authorities are installing emergency street telephones and struggling to maintain basic services.

Ukraine’s New Drones Turn Russian Supply Routes Into Hunting Grounds — Ukraine’s new mid-range strike drones are opening a new battlespace behind Russian lines, targeting supply routes once considered safe. The drones are disrupting logistics, expanding Ukraine’s geographic attack envelope and forcing Russia to defend a growing number of vulnerable areas.

Pro-Trump Influencer Laura Loomer Visits Ukraine, Changes Tone on Russia — Laura Loomer, a pro-Trump influencer and former Ukraine critic, has visited Ukraine and apologized for her previous pro-Kremlin rhetoric, saying she was a victim of Russian propaganda as she began to hit back at Kremlin messaging during the past few months.

For Ukraine’s Drones, Names Are Part of the Battle — Ukrainian drone makers are turning dark humour into a weapon, giving their systems names that mock Russia and boost morale. From the “Pissioun” interceptor to the “Liutyi” strike drone, the names have become symbols of resistance as Kyiv expands its drone war.

Fire Erupts Near Russia’s Largest Steel Plant After Reported Drone Attack in Lipetsk — A fire broke out near Russia’s largest steel producer, Novolipetsk Steel, in Lipetsk after residents reported explosions and a possible drone attack overnight. Russian officials confirmed a fire at industrial facilities but did not acknowledge an attack, while Ukraine has not commented.

Zelensky Weighs Replacing Syrsky With Drapaty Amid Military Leadership Crisis – Bloomberg — Volodymyr Zelensky is considering replacing Ukraine’s top military commander Oleksandr Syrsky with Maj. Gen. Mykhailo Drapaty amid a deepening crisis in the country’s defense leadership. The reported discussions come after the dismissal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov triggered the largest protests of Zelensky’s presidency.

IMF Approves $690 million for War-Torn Ukraine After Review — The International Monetary Fund’s board completed a review of Ukraine’s financing arrangement, clearing the way for immediate access to about $690 million, the Fund said on Monday.

Former SBU Special Forces Chief Takes Over Ukraine’s Defense Ministry Amid Fedorov Fallout — Former SBU Special Forces chief Yevhen Khmara took over as Ukraine’s acting defense minister on July 20 following President Volodymyr Zelensky’s decision to appoint him to the role. The move comes as protests continue over the dismissal of reformist Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov.

Sanctioning Russia is Popular in America — A bipartisan survey shows overwhelming US support for tougher measures against Russia, with strong backing for sanctions, actions against officials involved in abducting Ukrainian children, and penalties on foreign companies doing business with Moscow. Majorities across Republicans, Democrats, and independents also favor expanding US–Ukraine defense cooperation.

Zelensky Faces Deepening Political Crisis as Protests Dig In — President Volodymyr Zelensky faces mounting political pressure as protests over the dismissal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov enter a fifth day. Demonstrators demand military reforms and the removal of Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrsky, while the government weighs changes to avoid deepening divisions during the war.

Crimea Installs Landline Payphones as Mobile Blackouts Persist — Russian occupation authorities in Crimea have begun installing public payphones after scheduled mobile network shutoffs and Ukrainian strikes left residents without communication. The devices reportedly work even without electricity and connect free of charge to emergency services.

Syrsky Breaks Silence, Apologizes to Ousted Defense Minister Fedorov — Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) Oleksandr Syrsky apologized to former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, saying he only learned of their conflict after it became public. Fedorov's dismissal last week has sparked protests since, renewing questions about President Volodymyr Zelensky’s military command.

Zelensky, UK’s Burnham to Discuss Anti-Ballistic Coalition Cooperation at Upcoming Meeting — President Volodymyr Zelensky spoke with the UK’s new prime minister, Andy Burnham, thanking him for continued support for Ukraine. Both agreed to meet soon to discuss expanding cooperation, including within the Anti-Ballistic Coalition.

Russian Strike Hits Civilian Enterprise in Odesa, Kills 6, Wounds 6 — A Russian strike on a civilian enterprise in the Odesa region killed six people and injured another six, with the attack sparking fires and damaging a gas pipeline. Rescue operations were still underway.

Russian Strikes on Dnipropetrovsk Region Kill 2, Injure 17, Including Children — Russian armed forces struck four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 40 times on Monday, killing two people and injuring 17, including children as young as 1 year old. Residential apartments and other civilian infrastructure were damaged across multiple communities.

Lockheed Martin Unveils Cheaper Patriot Interceptor, PAC-3 ACE — As global demands surge, Lockheed Martin introduced the PAC-3 ACE, a Patriot interceptor designed to deter air and missile threats at less than half the cost of the PAC-3 MSE. The launch comes as Ukraine faces critical shortages of ballistic missile defense.

IN PHOTOS: What Are Ukrainians Saying About Fedorov’s Dismissal? — As protests against Fedorov’s dismissal continued nationwide over the weekend, the messages on protesters’ placards offered a not-so-subtle indication of what Ukrainians want – and, more subtly, how they believe the war for the country’s survival should be fought as it enters its fifth year.

Ukraine’s Game of Drones — The removal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov triggered criticism at home and abroad, with supporters crediting him for Ukraine’s wartime technological advances. However, Ukraine’s dominance in drone warfare will continue under newly appointed Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara, a security and drone operations specialist.

Budanov Says Public ‘Heard’ as Zelensky Holds Marathon Talks With Ukraine's Top Commanders — Budanov said public concerns over Fedorov's dismissal had been heard and urged calm as Zelensky held another round of meetings with Ukraine's top military commanders. The consultations come amid continued protests and speculation over changes in the military leadership.

Ukraine's Next Drone Weapon Is a Boat That Launches FPV Swarms — Ukraine's Omega Special Purpose Center has developed a new unmanned boat capable of launching FPV drones, supporting combat divers, and intercepting aerial threats. The platform is designed to extend strike range and strengthen Ukraine's growing fleet of naval unmanned systems.

Withering, Relentless Ukraine Drone Strike Campaign Hits Crimea Hard — Ukraine’s drone forces have spent the past two weeks hammering Russian logistics networks supporting occupied Crimea, targeting fuel tankers, cargo ships, ferries, power infrastructure, rail hubs, bridges, and freight traffic. The operation is aimed at isolating Crimea from mainland Russia and degrading its value as a military base.

Russia Struggles to Staff New Drone Force as Military Recruitment Falters – Report — Russia has failed to recruit the planned number of personnel for its new Unmanned Systems Forces, with only 8,000 specialists trained by mid-2026 instead of the expected 34,400, according to CIT. The shortfall comes as Russia faces a broader slowdown in military recruitment.

Russia Uses More Jet-Powered Drones, S8000 Banderol Missiles in Latest Attacks — The spokesperson of the Ukrainian Air Force said Russia has increasingly relied on its jet-powered drones and the S8000 Banderol missiles in its barrage against Ukraine, with previous reports suggesting the Banderol to be largely a product of foreign-supplied components.

Ukraine Opens New Front in Drone Warfare With Sea-Launched FPV Strike — Ukraine's marines used Barracuda drone boats to launch FPV drones against Russian positions near occupied Zaliznyi Port. Despite losing one USV to four Lancet strikes, the mission successfully hit Russian troops, equipment, and logistics.

Has Life Been Found on Mars? — Life on Mars is almost a certainty, argues biologist Steve Benner, whose new book challenges decades of NASA orthodoxy. Re‑examining Viking mission data, he shows the landers’ life‑detection experiments were positive and that later discoveries undermine earlier dismissals. Could it be that life on Earth did not originate here after all?

Seven PMs Since January 2016: Britain’s Decade of ‘Chaos’ — Andy Burnham is set to become Britain’s seventh prime minister since 2016 after Keir Starmer resigned following plunging approval ratings and mounting pressure within Labour. Burnham takes office pledging to restore political stability after a decade marked by rapid leadership turnover under both major parties.

Ukraine Targets Russian Online Retailer — Ukrainian drone strikes on Wildberries logistics centers in Russia, which reportedly killed eight people, have sparked debate over their legitimacy. Supporters argue the facilities have military value because they supply dual-use goods, while critics say the attacks mainly harm small businesses and civilians, who bear the economic costs of the war.

Trump Pushes for Iran's Inclusion in Graham’s Sanctions Bill — Trump had called on the US Congress to include Iran-related provisions in the Sanction Russia Act in honor of late US Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, who championed the bill. Vamos, España! Such Football is Needed by the World — The victory of the Spanish national team in the World Cup final against Argentina became a triumph of playing philosophy over pragmatic calculation. Luis De la Fuente built a system where intensive pressing, compactness, and an analytical approach completely neutralize the opponent. The Spaniards revived true football of intellect, and the absolute advantage in the decisive match proved that Luis de la Fuente's coaching ideas are unsurpassed.

Russia claimed it intercepted 381 Ukrainian drones.

Russian Strike on Turkish Cargo Ship Leaving Odesa Kills 10 — A Russian missile struck the Turkish-owned cargo ship Golden Leo as it departed Odesa with grain, killing 10 people. Ukraine says the attack targeted civilian shipping and comes amid an intensifying campaign against Black Sea ports and maritime exports.

The Follies of Historical Memory: Poland, Ukraine and the Politics of Selective Remembrance — Bohdan Vitvitsky argues that recent criticism from Polish politicians over Ukraine’s commemoration of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA) risks damaging relations at a time when both countries share vital security interests. Russian Anti-War Politician Ends Political Campaign After Pressure from Kremlin — Russian opposition politician Boris Nadezhdin has withdrawn from the September State Duma election after authorities blocked his campaign, labeled him a “foreign agent,” fined him over alleged extremist symbols, and restricted his movements. Nadezhdin said mounting pressure made it impossible to continue legally without putting his supporters, campaign team, and family at risk.

Farnborough 2026: Drones, Fighter Jets and Sovereignty — The Farnborough Airshow opens Monday with a strong focus on European rearmament, next-generation fighter jets, drones, and defense autonomy. Ukraine will showcase its battlefield-tested drone technologies, while Boeing seeks to restore confidence and highlight its MQ-28 Ghost Bat autonomous combat drone alongside delayed commercial aircraft programs.

Ukraine’s Massive 400-Drone Raid Hits Moscow Region Logistics Network, Fuel Sites — More than 400 drones targeted the Moscow region overnight, according to Russian officials, as Ukraine struck logistics hubs, an oil depot, and a residential building. The attack marked the second reported strike on a Wildberries warehouse in three days.

Zelensky to Hold ‘Key Talks’ on Strategy to End War Monday — President Volodymyr Zelensky announced in his Sunday evening address that he expects to hold “key conversations” on Monday regarding the strategy to conclude the war on acceptable terms. The announcement follows a weekend of extensive consultations with experienced military commanders, including Mykhailo Drapatyi, Volodymyr Horbatiuk, and Oleh Apostol, to assess battlefield conditions and future operations.

Estonian Foreign Minister Calls for Deeper Sanctions Against Russia — Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna has called for intensified pressure and tougher sanctions against Russia following a massive overnight ballistic missile attack on Kyiv. Polish Authorities Investigate Assault on Ukrainian Teenager for Speaking Native Language — A district prosecutor’s office in Płock, Poland, has launched an investigation into the physical and verbal assault of a 15-year-old Ukrainian boy who was attacked by an adult male on a city bus for speaking Ukrainian. The assailant reportedly struck the teenager and forced him and a companion off the vehicle.

Foreign Engineers for Ukraine: A Strategy for Victory? — Ukraine’s defense industry is producing military technology at an unprecedented pace, but a shortage of engineers and technical specialists is emerging as a major challenge. Attracting foreign talent could help increase production, accelerate innovation, strengthen knowledge transfer, and reinforce Ukraine’s position as a leader in defense technology.

Sanctions Busting? FIFA May pay World Cup Money to Russian Clubs — FIFA is planning to disburse a record $355 million through its Club Benefits Program following the 2026 World Cup. However, the organization faces potential legal action for reimbursing Russian clubs linked to sanctioned entities, such as Lukoil-owned Spartak Moscow. An investigation by the journalism platform Follow the Money revealed that FIFA previously paid $1.2 million to six Russian clubs after the 2022 tournament, potentia

Satellite Imagery Confirms Destruction of Russian Tu-95 Bomber at Engels Airbase — Satellite images from Planet Labs, published by the investigative project Schemes on July 19, confirm the destruction of a Russian Tu-95 strategic bomber at the Engels-2 military airbase in the Saratov region. The imagery shows the aircraft effectively severed in half, corroborating statements made by the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) regarding a long-range drone strike on July 17.

Russian Ballistic Missile Strike Destroys UKRTAC Military Gear Factory in Kyiv — A direct Russian missile strike completely destroyed the manufacturing facilities and warehouses of UKRTAC, a Ukrainian producer of military gear and personal protective equipment, during an attack on Kyiv on Sunday, July 19. Company founder Severion Dangadze confirmed the total destruction of the plant but reported no casualties among the staff. The strike occurred during a barrage involving approximately 40 ballis

Ukraine’s Children Are Rebuilding Their Futures Far From Home – We Must Not Fail Them Now — Ukrainian children displaced by Russia’s invasion are rebuilding their lives while carrying trauma, disrupted schooling and the struggle to preserve their language. Community schools like St Mary’s in London support more than 2,500 children, offering stability and cultural continuity, yet full‑time trauma‑focused provision still lacks funding. Moldova to Acquire Drone Interception Systems with EU Funding — Moldova’s Ministry of Defense will purchase new drone detection and interception systems backed by a €120 million ($137 million) EU assistance package. State Secretary of the Moldovan Ministry of Foreign Affairs Valeriu Mija stated that the country’s airspace has been violated 34 times by drones and missiles since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

US Completes Eighth Night of Strikes Against Iranian Military Facilities — US Central Command (CENTCOM) confirmed early Sunday that American forces completed an eighth consecutive night of strikes against Iranian military targets. The operations hit coastal surveillance and air defense facilities, maritime assets, and missile and drone storage sites. US forces also targeted elements of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) responsible for a July 17 attack on US personnel in Jordan.

Russian Strike on Kharkiv Suburbs Kills Three, Injures 20 — Russian forces attacked the suburbs of Kharkiv on Sunday, July 19, resulting in three civilian deaths and 20 people injured. Kharkiv Regional Military Administration Head Oleh Syniehubov reported that nine individuals were hospitalized, with three in serious condition. USF Commander Robert Brovdi reported that drones hit 13 electrical substations across occupied territories, including eight facilities in Crimea. Simultaneously, the Ukrainian General Staff confirmed strikes on four maritime assets linked to Russia’s shadow fleet – including tw

Kyiv Protests Grow: Calls to Reinstate Fedorov and Oust Ukraine’s Commander-in-Chief — Protests in Kyiv on Saturday, July 18, have expanded from calls to reinstate former Minister of Defense Mykhailo Fedorov to demands for the dismissal of Ukraine’s Commander-in-Chief, General Oleksandr Syrskyi. Protesters accuse Syrsky of obstructing military reforms and hindering the advancement of younger officers – allegations that gained momentum following Fedorov’s public criticism.

Ukrainian Railways (Ukrzaliznytsia) reported that a monitor group issued an early evacuation order, helping to prevent mass casualties, though one conductor sustained light injuries. Passengers were transferred to Zaporizhzhia via buses coordinated by the regional military administration.
